## Historical audit — S0124, chunk 1 of 2

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_163096530/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines in this file; character ranges are half-open.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 [0,5609) | The stated goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction of an indoor photograph, including camera, framing, proportions, occlusion and materials. The image itself is not visible in this audit, so its contents cannot be independently described. |
| Student response and execution, lines 3 [0,12084), 4 [0,12720) | The student’s *interpretation* was an old dormitory. Code constructed multiple objects: architecture, three left bunks, a foreground bunk, wardrobe, fireplace and smaller fittings. Bunk rails, posts and ladders were positioned as components; the fire guard was tilted. These are coded arrangements, not verified connections or poses. |
| Same response, line 3 [0,12084) | Code assigned colors, roughness and procedural noise/bump, and set a camera, two area lights and render settings. Whether textures were applied as intended and whether framing, illumination or geometry matched the photograph is unverified. |
| Execution result, line 5 [0,1970); student request, line 6 [0,19615) | Step 1 failed at `world.use_nodes`: the scene world was `None`; no image was returned. The next student request actually contained the traceback and a request to fix errors. This was runner feedback, not visible teacher advice. |
| Student response, line 8 [0,12526); execute, line 9 [0,13161) | The revised complete program creates a world when missing. It also changes floor grain, arch-stone rotation, bucket geometry and material processing. Step 2 executed that revision. |
| Execution result, line 10 [0,194012); select, line 11 [0,59) | Step 2 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and was selected. The log reports 16 render samples although the program requested 48. This establishes operational success for that step, not visual or geometric correctness. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, execution or receipt is visible in this chunk. The student independently produced and revised code in response to the execution error; the two recorded model sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2 and 7). No visual comparison by the student is visible here.

**Outcome and lessons.** The visible sequence is a technical failure followed by a successful build/render and selection—not an empty patch. Overall formal success and scene correctness remain **unknown**, because chunk 2 and the images are unavailable. A transferable observation is that explicit initialization of a missing Blender world preceded a successful rerun; this does not prove scene fidelity. The dormitory layout and object choices are task-specific hypotheses. Unresolved questions include whether the rendered objects, their contacts and orientations, materials, camera and lighting match the reference, and whether any later review or correction occurred.
